instructor: Mrs. Larlar is a valuable instructor for the department and is experienced in storytelling and narrative. However, we sent her several emails asking for feedback, including after she told us to change our idea and reach out again, but we never got a reply. She mostly focuses on the story and rarely comments on cinematography. There were times when the films were clearly out of focus, but she didn’t mention it, and instead gave very detailed criticism about the theme. I understand that narrative is her main area, but sometimes it feels like she doesn’t appreciate anything and mostly gives negative feedback, which can be discouraging. course: This is the final studio course of our department, but in my opinion, it was also the most inefficient. We only completed three projects. We spent almost two months working on the midterm music video, but only had about three weeks for the final short film, which deserved much more time and attention. Some projects were given too much time, while others were rushed. The final project had only one feedback session, and it felt too long and not helpful. Overall, the feedback throughout the course wasn’t very effective, it often felt draining or even personal, rather than constructive. It didn’t feel like we learned anything new or built our skills or portfolios in a meaningful way. Pre-production and production phases were given too much time, while post-production was short. Another issue is the focus of the studio courses overall. I don’t think every student should be expected to fully understand or take part in the filmmaking process. This is a Communication and Design department, not a film school. These high-credit studio courses should be split into different tracks by the second year, so students can focus on their strengths,  not everyone should be forced to make films.
